facts.text: I want a detailed recap of each part of a sales call transcript using a sales framework.
The transcript part I provided is labeled “Transcript part 3 (10m28s-20m4s our of 29m02s)”.
Matt Brown said a “wall to wall” deployment would hook into Okta and set up everyone.
Matt Brown said a “wall to wall” deployment would mean users are billable users.
Matt Brown said a partial rollout in stages can be done by providing a CSV list of users.
Matt Brown said imported users would be paid users while access is opened for organic growth from other teams.
Matt Brown said there are options including a full wall to wall deployment right away.
Matt Brown said an organic rollout would use a quarterly true up system.
Matt Brown said the quarterly true up example starts at 500 users and increases to 750 the next quarter.
Nick Sarkesian asked how the quarterly true up works with 500 enterprise licenses and 600 users on a free version.
Nick Sarkesian asked whether additional enterprise licenses (another 100) can be added mid-quarter.
Nick Sarkesian asked how billing is determined at the end of the quarter based on how long additional users use the licenses.
Matt Brown said access cannot be split into 500 enterprise and 100 pro 53; it is all or nothing from that perspective.
Matt Brown said after agreeing on a rollout, the plan is flat rate for additional users added to Fellow.
Matt Brown said additional users can be added without bottlenecks like contacting an account manager or messaging support.
Matt Brown said additional users can be added on the day they are added and billing adjusts when the billing period comes up.
Matt Brown said quarterly true up involves checking who has been active in the last period and adjusting accordingly.
Trina Berks asked whether billing can go backwards if 600 people use it but later only 500 remain.
Trina Berks asked about reducing from 600 users back to 500.
Matt Brown said clawing back would be a missed opportunity for both parties.
Matt Brown said the objective is not to overbuild and then claw it back.
Matt Brown said they want to start with users already committed to it right away.
Matt Brown said Fellow ramp-up resources exist to build initial momentum.
Matt Brown said adoption is described as “pretty viral” once team members show it to other team members.
Trina Berks said if OCTA is used, people may click on it twice and then never touch it again.
Matt Brown said they can tell who is an active user versus who has only signed in once.
Matt Brown said they can look back and determine how many users are using it on an active basis (example mentioned: 500 users).
Matt Brown said they will send security compliance documentation in a recap packet.
Matt Brown said they will send more about TA integration.
Matt Brown said SOC to Mbda will be sent over for DocuSign signature.
Matt Brown said they will send JIRA integration information.
Matt Brown asked whether the team wants initial pricing based on scope or deployment or whether it is too premature.
Eric Cameron said they would activate pro licenses in the short term for users they are holding on billing for.
Eric Cameron said they want Nick and the team to feel good about the documentation before making enterprise-level decisions.
Matt Brown said there is a 30-day robust methodology to get everyone from the paid license perspective up and running.
Eric Cameron said they probably would not fully kick off at an enterprise level until the beginning of next year.
Matt Brown said in the meantime they can build momentum with already converted advocates of Fellow and collaborate with team members who might not have seen it yet.
Eric Cameron said billing was paused and that there are active users for the past month.
Eric Cameron said there are 20 users already going back.
Matt Brown said he can flip billing to a pro annual rate.
Matt Brown said additional users can be invited by other current paid users or alternatively access can be restricted.
Matt Brown asked how the workspace configuration should be handled for inviting users.
Eric Cameron said it is fine to come in through him, but coming in through the team makes more sense long term.
Nick Sarkesian said both options make sense and that if one of them is unavailable, the other can be used.
Matt Brown said Tyler and Alex are the only two admins at that point in time.
Matt Brown said he can make Nick, Trina, and the other requested people admins as well.
Matt Brown recommended keeping admin access open to encourage organic growth in the short term.
Eric Cameron asked whether Tyler and Alex’s admin access can be removed and Nick and Trina added as admins.
Matt Brown said Alex is fine with removing his admin access and that he and Matt talked about it.
Matt Brown said he will send an email confirmation after the recap to confirm the admin changes are completed.
Eric Cameron asked if anyone else has questions.
Nick Sarkesian said “All right. Thanks. I appreciate it. Thanks so much. Have a great day. Bye. Feel.”

keyphrases: beginning of next year enterprise kickoff

events.text: Quarterly true up rollout example discussed: start at 500 users and bump to 750 next quarter.
Discussion of end-of-quarter billing adjustment based on active usage of additional licenses.
Billing paused; active users for the past month and 20 users already going back.
Enterprise rollout kickoff timing: not fully kick off until the beginning of next year.
Onboarding methodology timing: 30-day robust methodology to get paid-license users up and running.
Admin changes: remove Tyler and Alex admins and add Nick and Trina as admins; email confirmation after recap.
